opennyai_summary.final__facts:
This is an appeal challenging the award passed by the reference Court i.e. Civil Judge Senior Division, Bhusawal dated 05th September, 2019, by which several land references were decided.
So far as present appeal is concerned, the relevant land reference would be in L.A.R. No. 535 of 2014 (Old L.A.R. No. 961 of 2007).
opennyai_summary.arguments:
2. Challenging the award passed by the reference Court, it is contended by learned counsel for the appellant/claimant that the sale-deeds, 903-FA-404-20.odt duly proved on record by the claimants,
were not taken into consideration on the ground that those three sale-deeds were of village Ainpur and Khirdi, whereas the land acquired was from Bhamalwadi.
Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the aforesaid sale-deeds ought to have been taken into consideration since those two villages were adjacent to village Bhamalwadi.
He submitted that the act of not producing best material in the form of evidence before the reference Court at the instance of acquiring body is deliberate act and what is required to be considered is the highest sale instance.
3. In order to buttress is contention, he has relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Mahesh Dattatray Thirthkar Vs. State of Maharashtra, reported in AIR 2009 SC 2238, more particularly paragraph nos. 27, 29, 30 and 32, wherein the Apex Court has held that burden of 903-FA-404-20.odt proving the true market value of acquired property is on the State that has acquired it for a particular purpose.
4. He has also relied upon the judgment reported in 2008 (3) AIR Bom R 632 in Executive Engineer,
P.W.D. VI (R & B)m Margaon and Anr. Vs. Versus Antonion Almeida and Ors., more particularly paragraph nos. 11 and 12, wherein this Court has stated that for determination of market value,
comparable sale instances are required to be taken into consideration and if there are dissimilarities in regard to locality, shape, size or nature between land covered by sales and land acquired, it is open to the Court to proportionately reduce compensation for acquired land than what is reflected in the sales depending upon disadvantages attached with acquired land.
5. In order to take his argument to the logical end, learned counsel for the appellant has also invited my attention to the case of Special Tahsildar (RC) Vs. Chithra & Ors. reported in 2010 1 MLJ 861 and has contended that the market value of the acquired land is required to be determined based on the comparable sales method and higher value reflected in those sales should be adopted as the market value of the acquired land.
903-FA-404-20.odt 6. Per contra, learned counsel for the acquiring body has submitted that the reference Court has taken into consideration various aspects, and therefore, intervention at the hands of this Court is not required.

As far as the judgments cited supra and the law laid down by various Courts cannot be disputed at all, suffice it to say every case will differ 903-FA-404-20.odt on its own fact.
